Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflated lungs with increased anterior-posterior diameter, no evidence of infiltrates or masses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you notice any wheezing or shortness of breath when you exert yourself?

REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry: FEV1 65% of predicted, FVC 78% of predicted, FEV1/FVC Ratio 0.60 (reduced).

speaker: Doctor
text: Are your symptoms worse in the morning or evening, and do you have a history of allergies, asthma, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: My symptoms seem to be about the same throughout the day, though I do feel quite short of breath when I'm active. Yes, I have a long history of smoking, though I don't have any diagnosed asthma or seasonal allergies that I can recall. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; given your smoking history and the spirometry showing a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio, do you currently experience chronic phlegm production or frequent respiratory infections?

DIAGNOSIS READY: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
